CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH RAI K  ORAL ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.97/2022 (arising out of Crime No.133/2021), registered by Devara Hipparagi Police, for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506(2) r/w Section 34 of IPC,
pending on the file of Civil Judge and JMFC, Sindagi, Vijayapur.
2.
The factual matrix of the case is that, respondent No.2 married one Rajakumar Tukaram on 18.04.2013.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:764 HC-KAR Thereafter, she was residing along with him at Hitnalli Tanda.
Out of the wedlock, they begotten two children.

According to respondent No.2, the petitioners i.e.,
accused No.2 and 3 is her brother-in-law and his wife and they are residing adjacent to her house.
After sometime, her husband-accused No.1 started to harass her both physically and mentally for additional dowry of Rs.2,00,000/-.
The petitioners also instigated accused No.1 for his act of harassment.
On 01.08.2021 at about 03:00 p.m., accused No.1 assaulted respondent No.2 with an iron rod to bring additional dowry from her parents.
According to her, the petitioners were also present at that time and they also abused and assaulted her.

3. On the strength of the said complaint, the respondent-Police registered the case in Crime No.133/2021 dated 08.08.2021 for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 504 and 506 Shivanand vs The State Of Karnataka on 30 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195586348/
2 r/w Section 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: Subsequently, respondent No.1-Police conducted the investigation laid charge sheet against this petitioners and another by arraying these petitioners as accused No.2 and 3 for the aforementioned offences.

Accordingly, the learned Magistrate took cognizance NC:
2026:KHC-K:764 HC-KAR of the offences and issued summons to the accused including these petitioners.
Hence, this petition.

4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
5.

Apart from urging several contentions, learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the petitioners being accused Nos.2 and 3, are residing separately from the matrimonial house of respondent No.2.

Nevertheless, in the further statement of respondent No.2 recorded by respondent No.1-Police, she has categorically stated that these petitioners were not participated in the alleged incident and by mistakenly, she had mentioned their name in the complaint.

According to him,
except the omnibus allegations made in the statement of other witnesses, absolutely no other prima facie materials are placed against these petitioners by the prosecution.
Accordingly, prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 contended that, now respondent No.1-Police have investigated and laid charge sheet against the petitioners and another.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:764 HC-KAR
Hence, the proceedings cannot be quashed against the petitioners and the petition is liable to be dismissed.
7. Learned High Court Government Pleader opposed the petition and prays to dismiss the same.
8. I have given my anxious consideration both on the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the charge sheet materials.
9. As could be gathered from records, it is specifically stated in the complaint that respondent No.2 is residing along with her husband, two children and her father-in-law at Hitnalli Thanda.
These petitioners being her brother-in-law and his wife, are residing separately in the said village.

Further,
on careful perusal of the further statement of respondent No.2, she specifically stated that on the alleged date of incident i.e., 01.08.2021, though these petitioners were present at the scene of occurrence, they neither abused nor assaulted her, as stated by her in the complaint.
As per the other allegation in the complaint is concerned, it is clear that accused No.1-husband alone, harassed her to bring additional dowry of Rs.2,00,000/-.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:764 HC-KAR 10.

In such circumstance, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of K. Subba Rao vs. State of Telangana represented by its Secretary, Department of Home and Others reported in 2024 INSC 960, at paragraph No.6 held that the Court should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

sentences.text: It is also settled position of law that if a person is made to face a criminal trial on some general and sweeping allegations without bringing on record any specific instances of criminal conduct, it is nothing but abuse of process of the Court

. The Courts pose a duty to subject the allegation levelled in the complaint to a thorough scrutiny to find out, whether there is any gain of truth in the allegations or whether they are made only with the sole object of involving certain individuals in a criminal charge, more particularly when a prosecution arise from a matrimonial dispute.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:764 HC-KAR 11.

Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Dara Lakshmi Narayan vs. State of Telangana reported in 2025 (3) SCC 735, held in para Nos.25 and 28 as under:
"25.

entities.text: Dara Lakshmi Narayan vs. State of Telangana reported in 2025 (3) SCC 735
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A mere reference to the names of family members in a criminal case arising out of a matrimonial dispute, without specific allegations indicating their active involvement should be nipped in the bud.

It is a well-recognised fact, borne out of judicial experience, that there is often a tendency to implicate all the members of the husband's family when domestic disputes arise out of a matrimonial discord.
Such generalised and sweeping accusations unsupported by concrete evidence or particularized allegations cannot form the basis for criminal prosecution.
Courts must exercise caution in such cases to prevent misuse of legal provisions and the legal process and avoid unnecessary harassment of innocent family members.

In the present case, appellant Nos.2 to 6, who are the members of the family of appellant No.1 have been living in different cities and have not resided in the matrimonial house of appellant No.1 and respondent No.2 herein.
Hence, they cannot be dragged into criminal prosecution and the same would be an abuse of the process of the law in the absence of specific allegations made against each of them.
28. The inclusion of Section 498A of the IPC by way of an amendment was intended to curb cruelty inflicted on a woman by her husband and his family, ensuring swift intervention by the State.

However, in recent years, as there have been a notable rise in matrimonial disputes across the country, NC: 2026:KHC-K:764 HC-KAR accompanied by growing discord and tension within the institution of marriage,
consequently, there has been a growing tendency to misuse provisions like Section 498A of the IPC as a tool for unleashing personal vendetta against the husband and his family by a wife.

Making vague and generalised allegations during matrimonial conflicts, if not scrutinized, will lead to the misuse of legal processes and an encouragement for use of arm twisting tactics by a wife and/or her family.
Sometimes, recourse is taken to invoke Section 498A of the IPC against the husband and his family in order to seek compliance with the unreasonable demands of a wife.

Consequently, this Court has, time and again, cautioned against prosecuting the husband and his family in the absence of a clear prima facie case against them."

sentences.text: Applying the above findings of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the above cases to the fact and circumstances of this case, except the omnibus allegations against these petitioners, there are no such specific averments made against these petitioners that they are involved in the alleged offences.
Hence, in my considered view, continuation of criminal proceedings against these petitioners is an abuse of process of Court.

Though the entire allegations made in the charge sheet taken into consideration on its face value also, no prima facie NC: 2026:KHC-K:764 HC-KAR case is made out against these petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is allowed.

ii. The proceedings against the  petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 in  C.C.No.97/2022 (Crime No.133/2021),
registered by Devara Hipparagi Police, for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506(2) r/w Section 34 of IPC, pending on the file of Civil Judge and JMFC, Sindagi, Vijayapur, is hereby quashed.
